subject: mathematics
question_text: Show that the determinant with rows (a+b+2c, a, b), (c, b+c+2a, b) and (c, a, c+a+2b) is equal to 2(a+b+c)³.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.24 — LAQ chapter 3 Matrices, answer 14, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page), and the book's self-declared 'No.2 in Dets'. The four printed appearance tags (TS 16,19 · AP 16,18) make it the most-asked determinant in the chapter. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S. This page carries a 'Tick Boxes' widget in the margin where the [N Marks] tags would normally sit, so no split is printed for this question. The 2+1+2+1+1 above is inferred from the split the same book DOES print for answer 17 on book p.26 — a structurally identical proof (sum a row or column, take the common factor out, two row operations, expand) which is printed as 1+1+1+2+1+1. The two marks on the opening column operation reflect that spotting C₁+C₂+C₃ is the whole question; a teacher may well weight it differently. Star rank is the CHAPTER's ★★★, not this question's. Paper position: Maths-1A Section C runs Q18-Q24 at 7 marks each, answer any 5 of 7. Re-cut to the 8-mark Section-C form of the 2026-27 pattern (TGBIE model paper w.e.f. 2026-27): the extra mark goes to the "Column operation C₁ → C₁+C₂+C₃" step.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say which rows or columns you add together first, what comes out common, and how the determinant finishes.

steps.label: Write the determinant
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Before writing anything else, add the three entries of any row in your head — each row sums to 2(a+b+c). That is the whole question in one observation.
steps.memory_tip: Add the three entries of any ROW in your head — each sums to 2(a+b+c). That is the whole question.

lines.text: \Delta = \begin{vmatrix} a+b+2c & a & b \\ c & b+c+2a & b \\ c & a & c+a+2b \end{vmatrix}

recall.must_convey: That the working starts from the given determinant. Naming it is full credit.
accept: write the given determinant first
take delta as the determinant in the question
start with the LHS determinant
modata ichina determinant rasta
write down the determinant we have to prove

steps.why: Every entry is built from a, b and c, and the answer is a power of (a+b+c). That match is the signal to add rows or columns together rather than to expand.
common_mistakes: Expanding the 3×3 determinant directly, which produces a page of terms.
Trying row subtraction first; there is nothing to cancel yet.

steps.label: Add all three columns into C₁
steps.margin_note: Three of the eight marks, and the only idea in the question. Adding C₂ and C₃ into C₁ makes every entry of column 1 the same: 2a+2b+2c. Nothing else in the proof is hard.
steps.memory_tip: Adding C₂ and C₃ into C₁ makes every entry of column 1 the same: 2a+2b+2c.

lines.text: \Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 2a{+}2b{+}2c & a & b \\ 2a{+}2b{+}2c & b+c+2a & b \\ 2a{+}2b{+}2c & a & c+a+2b \end{vmatrix}

recall.must_convey: That columns 2 and 3 are added into column 1, and that this makes all three entries of column 1 equal to 2a+2b+2c.
accept: add column two and column three to column one so every entry becomes two a plus two b plus two c
apply C one goes to C one plus C two plus C three and the first column becomes identical
sum all three columns into the first column and each entry is two into a plus b plus c
C1 ki C2 and C3 kalipithe anni entries two a plus two b plus two c avthai
add the columns together and the first column becomes the same value three times
reject: apply C one plus C two
heard_as: two a plus two b plus two c

steps.why: Adding other columns into one column never changes a determinant's value. It is worth doing when it makes a whole column identical — because an identical column can be taken out as a common factor.
common_mistakes: Adding rows instead of columns; here the columns are what sum to the same value.
Adding into C₂ or C₃ instead of C₁, which works but makes the next step harder to see.
Writing a+b+c instead of 2a+2b+2c — check the sum, every row has a 2 in it.

steps.label: Take 2(a+b+c) common
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Column 1 is now 2(a+b+c) three times over, so that factor comes out and column 1 becomes 1, 1, 1.
steps.memory_tip: 2(a+b+c) comes out of column 1, leaving it as 1, 1, 1.

lines.text: \Delta = 2(a{+}b{+}c) \begin{vmatrix} 1 & a & b \\ 1 & b+c+2a & b \\ 1 & a & c+a+2b \end{vmatrix}

recall.must_convey: That 2(a+b+c) is taken common out of column 1, leaving 1, 1, 1 in that column.
accept: take two into a plus b plus c common from the first column leaving ones
pull out two a plus b plus c so the first column becomes one one one
the common factor two into a plus b plus c comes outside
first column nunchi two into a plus b plus c common teeste ones migulutai
take the two and the a plus b plus c out in front of the determinant
reject: take a plus b plus c common
heard_as: two a plus b plus c

steps.why: The 2 that comes out here is the 2 in the answer 2(a+b+c)³. Losing it is the commonest way to finish this question with (a+b+c)³ and drop marks.
common_mistakes: Taking only (a+b+c) out and leaving the 2 behind.
Taking the factor out of a row instead of the column.
Cubing the factor here; it comes out once.

steps.label: Do R₂−R₁ and R₃−R₁
steps.margin_note: Two more marks. Column 1 is all 1s now, so subtracting row 1 clears it. What is left is a triangular determinant — zeros below the diagonal — and those are read straight off.
steps.memory_tip: Column 1 is all 1s, so subtracting row 1 clears it, leaving a TRIANGULAR determinant.
lines: R₂ → R₂ − R₁ and R₃ → R₃ − R₁:

recall.must_convey: That row 1 is subtracted from rows 2 and 3, and that this leaves (a+b+c) on the diagonal with zeros elsewhere in those rows.
accept: subtract row one from row two and row three leaving a plus b plus c on the diagonal
apply R two minus R one and R three minus R one and the determinant becomes diagonal
do the row subtractions and you get a plus b plus c twice down the diagonal with zeros
R2 minus R1 and R3 minus R1 cheste diagonal lo a plus b plus c vasthundi
take row one away from the lower two rows and only the diagonal entries are left
reject: apply R two minus R one

steps.why: b − b = 0 in row 2 and a − a = 0 in row 3. Those cancellations are why the middle and last entries collapse, and they only happen because the first row was subtracted, not added.
common_mistakes: Subtracting in the wrong order and picking up minus signs on the diagonal.
Missing that the off-diagonal entries cancel to zero and carrying them along.

steps.label: Expand along the first column
steps.margin_note: Sixth mark. Column 1 is 1, 0, 0 so only one term survives, and its minor is a 2×2 with zeros off the diagonal — its value is just the product of the diagonal.
steps.memory_tip: Column 1 is 1, 0, 0, so one term survives and its minor has zeros off the diagonal.

recall.must_convey: That expanding along the first column leaves one term, whose 2×2 minor is (a+b+c) times (a+b+c).
accept: expand along the first column and the two by two minor is a plus b plus c squared
only the one contributes so we get a plus b plus c into a plus b plus c
the minor is diagonal so its value is the product of the diagonal entries
first column lo one zero zero kabatti oke term vasthundi
expand and the small determinant gives a plus b plus c whole squared
heard_as: a plus b plus c squared

steps.why: A determinant with zeros below the diagonal is the product of its diagonal entries. Every operation before this line existed to reach that shape.
common_mistakes: Expanding along a row instead of the column of zeros and doing three times the work.

steps.label: State the result
steps.margin_note: Last mark. One factor of (a+b+c) came from the column, two more from the diagonal — three in all, and the 2 that came out with them.
steps.memory_tip: One factor from the column and two from the diagonal — three in all, plus the 2.
lines: One (a+b+c) from C₁ and two from the minor:

recall.must_convey: That the three factors of (a+b+c) multiply to the cube and the 2 stays in front, giving 2(a+b+c)³.
accept: three factors of a plus b plus c give the cube and the two stays outside so it is two into a plus b plus c cubed
one from the column and two from the minor make a plus b plus c cubed times two
the answer is two a plus b plus c whole cubed
moodu a plus b plus c factors kalipithe cube avthundi and two bayata untundi
multiply the factors to get two into a plus b plus c cube which is the RHS
heard_as: a plus b plus c cubed

steps.why: Counting where each (a+b+c) came from is the check that catches a dropped factor. If you can only account for two, the 2 or a diagonal entry went missing.
common_mistakes: Writing 2(a+b+c)² by forgetting the factor that came out of the column.

insider_note: Add all three COLUMNS into C₁ and every entry becomes 2(a+b+c) — the 2 in the answer comes from there, not from the final expansion. Row subtractions then leave a diagonal.
